summary: Builds the people, partnerships, funding and operating infrastructure King’s needs to create high-quality experiential opportunities, connect students and graduates with employers in the UK and internationally, widen access to purposeful global experience, remove barriers to participation, and support successful transition into graduate futures.
detailSummary:
King’s already holds extensive relationships with employers, industry, public bodies, community and third-sector organisations, civic and cultural partners, international organisations and alumni. It also has strong careers expertise, an established Global Mobility service, pockets of student-opportunity funding, philanthropic relationships and locally developed processes for experiential activity. These assets are distributed across faculties and professional services and are not yet consistently visible, coordinated or activated as one coherent institutional engine for opportunity and graduate success.

The proposition therefore brings together six connected capabilities. First, King’s will preserve and strengthen the common operating infrastructure through which experiential opportunities are sourced, designed, approved, promoted, delivered, supported and evaluated. This includes clearer roles across central teams and faculties; proportionate standards for quality, accessibility, safeguarding, risk, data and student support; common templates and agreements; simpler contracting and payment routes; better partner intelligence; and a clearer institutional opportunity pipeline. Delivery remains distributed: the infrastructure should make local delivery easier, safer and more consistent rather than centralising it.

Second, King’s will establish a dedicated UK Experiential Partnerships & Opportunity Development team from September 2027 at the same planned staffing level as the fully developed international employer-engagement team. The model is 1 x G6 Experiential Partnerships & Opportunity Development Manager, 2 x G5 Experiential Opportunity Development Advisers and 1 x G5 Experiential Partnerships Operations & Intelligence Adviser, costing £214,089 annualised on the current fully loaded role-cost basis. The G6 will manage the UK experiential opportunity pipeline, triage and complex brokerage; the two Opportunity Development Advisers will work faculty-facing to turn external propositions into viable projects, placements, live briefs, challenges and related experiences; and the Operations & Intelligence Adviser will provide the shared partner-pipeline, onboarding, contracting/payment coordination, data, QA and evaluation backbone. The precise faculty or sector portfolios of the two development advisers should be informed by the first-year capability review and demand emerging through 2.1.4, 2.2.3 and 2.2.4. The team will work with existing Work-Based Experience and partnership leadership rather than duplicating it.

Third, King’s will protect and then grow international employer engagement across the full 2026/27 to 2028/29 investment window. The urgent continuity requirement begins in 2026/27: a G6 Employer Relations & Insights Manager (International) is modelled from October 2026 to protect existing employer relationships, market intelligence and in-country activity, followed by a G5 East Asia Adviser from January 2027 for the second half of the academic year. A £15,000 employer-facing and in-country activity budget supports this first year. Both roles then operate for the full 2027/28 year, when the international non-pay envelope rises to £50,000. In January 2029, the final two G5 Advisers extend capacity across South and South East Asia and Europe and North America, ensuring that the full four-post team is live before the end of mobilisation. This capability is intended to improve access to relevant employers and labour-market intelligence for students and graduates while also strengthening King’s employability proposition in strategically important recruitment markets.

Fourth, King’s will strengthen Global Mobility with two incremental opportunity-development posts from September 2027: one G6 and one G5. These roles are intended to add growth and translation capacity rather than duplicate the existing service’s core exchange administration. Working with the established Global Mobility team, faculties and King’s Edge, they will grow and broker a broader mix of purposeful outward mobility, including shorter-form, experiential, work-related and other accessible international opportunities; connect mobility more deliberately to skills and graduate futures; and help turn overseas partnerships and propositions into student-ready opportunities that can feed the flexible and near-curriculum offer.

Fifth, King’s will establish a small Graduate Transitions function from September 2028, comprising a G7 Head of Graduate Transitions and a G6 Graduate Transitions Coach. Deferring mobilisation until the final investment year keeps 2027/28 focused on opportunity generation and infrastructure while allowing the graduate-transition model, targeting logic and evidence base to be designed in advance. Once live, the function will move support beyond a predominantly reactive model by using Careers Readiness and other available data to identify graduates who may be at risk of poorer outcomes and provide targeted coaching, job-search support, employer referral and other interventions through the critical post-completion period captured by Graduate Outcomes.

Sixth, the deliverable will retain the existing access and opportunity-growth work. King’s will review and consolidate financial support for students undertaking employment-enhancing and developmental activity, with the intended direction of a coherent Student Opportunities Fund combining low-friction microbursaries of around £150-£250 with more substantial awards of around £4,000 for genuine out-of-pocket participation costs. Any new award pot sits outside the King’s Edge mobilisation ask and requires a separate institutional, consolidated-fund, philanthropic or other funding route. Alumni engagement and philanthropy will also be used deliberately to grow the supply of opportunity, including service-learning and social-good projects and models in which paid PhD project leads can mobilise flexible opportunities for wider student participation.

The causal logic is that King’s can create more meaningful and accessible experience, connect it more effectively to employers and graduate destinations, widen access to purposeful international experience, and improve institutional efficiency by joining up assets it already holds with targeted new capabilities. The fully mobilised Core resource proposition is £714,058 annualised: £214,089 UK Experiential Partnerships & Opportunity Development staffing, £214,089 international employer-engagement staffing, £126,265 Graduate Transitions staffing, £109,615 Global Mobility opportunity-development staffing and a £50,000 international employer-engagement non-pay envelope. For investment-case budgeting, the 2026/27 international continuity wave is modelled at £43,034 for the G6 from October, £26,119 for the East Asia G5 from January and £15,000 of non-pay activity. September starts in later years are modelled at ten months and January 2029 starts at six months. This produces a direct in-year profile of £84,153 in 2026/27, £429,369 in 2027/28 and £640,777 in 2028/29, or £1,154,299 across the three-year investment window. The £714,058 figure is the annualised exit run-rate once the complete operating model is live by June 2029, not an additional or fourth-year mobilisation budget. All grade-based staffing figures are treated as fully loaded planning costs including employer National Insurance and pension/superannuation and should be validated with Finance/HR before approval.

caseForChange.problem: King’s has substantial external relationships, careers expertise, an established Global Mobility service, alumni connection and pockets of student-opportunity funding, but the infrastructure that turns these assets into opportunity and positive graduate destinations is fragmented. Relationship management, opportunity design, contracting, risk, payments, partner intelligence, international employer engagement, global opportunity development, graduate support and financial-access mechanisms can operate separately. UK external relationships are not always translated into student-ready experiential opportunities at the scale required, and the institution has limited incremental capacity to grow and translate a broader portfolio of purposeful outward mobility beyond existing core provision. Existing international activity is particularly fragile because proven East Asia work is currently unsupported by dedicated resource. This creates duplicated effort, missed connections, uneven access, fragile international employer capability and a reactive transition model for graduates who need additional support.
caseForChange.opportunity: King’s can create a stronger institutional engine that connects UK experiential partnership and opportunity development, shared operating infrastructure, employer relationships, international labour-market capability, global mobility opportunity development, proactive graduate transition, alumni engagement, philanthropy and student financial support. Shared standards can reduce friction and duplication without centralising delivery. Immediate 2026/27 investment can protect the international activity already shown to work while the broader architecture is built. A four-post UK team, comprising one G6 manager, two G5 opportunity-development advisers and one G5 operations-and-intelligence adviser, can separate outward-facing opportunity creation from the shared operational work needed to make those opportunities safe, scalable and repeatable. Incremental Global Mobility capacity can grow shorter-form and employability-linked international opportunities without displacing the existing team’s core exchange work. A small Graduate Transitions function can then be introduced from September 2028 to target support where it is most needed. A coherent Student Opportunities Fund and philanthropic propositions can remove financial barriers and grow opportunity supply.
caseForChange.whyNow: King’s Edge is increasing the volume and ambition of experiential opportunity within and beyond the curriculum at the same time as the graduate labour market becomes more challenging and employability becomes more important to student choice. Existing East Asia employability activity has demonstrated value but is unsupported by dedicated resource, has displaced domestic employer-engagement capacity and faces a near-term continuity risk if investment waits until 2027/28. Growth through 2.1.4, 2.2.3 and 2.2.4 will also create additional demand for UK partner sourcing, brokerage, opportunity translation and shared operational support, including global opportunity as a thematic priority. The existing Global Mobility team already facilitates study abroad and overseas traineeships, but Edge creates a case for additional opportunity-development capacity focused on growth, accessibility and stronger connection to graduate futures. Graduate support remains largely reactive after completion. A phased investment profile beginning with urgent international protection in 2026/27 allows King’s to address these gaps while still ensuring the complete operating model is live by June 2029.
caseForChange.intendedChange: King’s moves from fragmented relationship, opportunity, funding and graduate-transition activity towards connected employability and experiential infrastructure. Existing international employer engagement is protected immediately through a G6 from October 2026, an East Asia G5 from January 2027 and an initial £15,000 activity budget; UK external relationships are converted into student-ready opportunities through a specified four-post Experiential Partnerships & Opportunity Development team from September 2027, combining faculty-facing opportunity creation with shared operations and intelligence; staff and partners work through clearer routes and common processes; international employer capability reaches its full four-post structure by June 2029; a broader range of students can access purposeful global experience; students have more consistent access to meaningful experience and financial support; and a proactive graduate-transition function is added from September 2028. King’s can then evidence both Education and Student Success benefits and wider recruitment and reputation benefits from the same institutional capability.

problemSolved: King’s does not yet consistently convert its distributed external relationships, employability capability, global partnerships, alumni connection and opportunity funding into a coherent supply of accessible UK and international experience and sustained support through the transition into graduate destinations.
whatChanges: King’s establishes connected UK experiential partnership and opportunity-development, international employer-engagement, global mobility, access and graduate-transition infrastructure that can generate and sustain more opportunities, reduce operational friction, widen purposeful international experience, remove financial barriers and intervene proactively where graduates need additional support.
